description: Source Registry entries backing the Housing category real-data import. These are seeded into the Source table by server/prisma/seed/data/sources.ts (upserted by name) — this file is a human-readable manifest of which sources back which metrics, not a separate ingestion path.

sources.name: American Community Survey
sources.note: No 1-year ACS estimates exist for 2020, and the 2025 1-year estimate is not yet released as of this import. Requires a data.census.gov API key as of 2026 (unkeyed requests now return 'Missing Key' even for single reads). Chicago's 2015-2019/2021-2024 figures were pulled directly from the api.census.gov ACS 1-year endpoint (place 1714000) with a user-supplied key: median_rent is B25064_001E directly; vacancy_rate is computed as vacant-for-rent (B25004_002E) divided by (vacant-for-rent + renter-occupied [B25003_003E]). Other jurisdictions' figures in this pass were compiled via published secondary citations, not direct API calls.

sources.name: State of New York City's Housing and Neighborhoods
sources.note: Used for NYC citywide median gross rent, which the Furman Center reports annually from ACS/NYCHVS data.

sources.name: Chicago Point-in-Time Count & Survey Report
sources.note: 2023 figure includes a large one-time increase attributable to newly arrived asylum seekers in city shelter — a real methodological discontinuity, not a data error.

sources.name: King County Point-in-Time Count
sources.note: County-wide, not city-of-Seattle-only; methodology changed from a literal count to statistical Respondent-Driven Sampling starting in 2022, and some years were skipped under HUD's every-other-year unsheltered-count schedule.

sources.name: State of the Cities Data Systems
sources.note: Identified as the right official source for these metrics, but not yet pulled into real MetricValue rows this pass. See per-jurisdiction CSV TODOs. housing_permits_issued was pulled directly from the Census Bureau's own BPS place files instead of this HUD mirror — see us_census_bps_place below.

sources.name: Building Permits
sources.note: City of Chicago Data Portal (Socrata), dataset ydr8-5enu. Median of the processing_time field (calendar days from application_start_date to issue_date), computed server-side via Socrata's median() aggregate, grouped by issue year. Each annual figure is backed by ~14,000-24,000 permit records across all permit types (signs, renovations, new construction, etc.) — not new-residential permits specifically, since this dataset doesn't cleanly separate residential unit permits from other permit types without unreliable text classification of work descriptions.

sources.name: Chicago Department of Housing Annual Report
sources.note: City of Chicago DOH Annual Report (2022 edition), 'Total units produced per year' chart, p. 16 (https://www.chicago.gov/content/dam/city/depts/doh/plans/Annual%20Report%20Final%208.29.23.pdf). No data table accompanies the chart, so 2015-2022 figures were derived by measuring bar-top pixel position against the chart's calibrated gridlines and rounding to the nearest 10 — imported as dataQuality=estimated, not official. housing_starts and housing_completions remain placeholder: no official or academic/alternative source publishes a city-level series for either (checked DePaul's Institute for Housing Studies, Chicago Rehab Network, and NHPD — none track annual starts/completions counts, and NHPD requires account registration to access its data).

sources.name: Building Permits Survey
sources.note: U.S. Census Bureau BPS place-level annual data files (Midwest Region, Chicago FIPS place 1714000), downloaded directly from www2.census.gov/econ/bps/Place/. Value is the sum of the 'Bldgs' (buildings authorized) column across all four structure-size categories (1-unit, 2-unit, 3-4 unit, 5+ unit) for the calendar year. The same rows also carry a 'Units' column (individual housing units authorized) that is substantially larger for Chicago due to large multifamily buildings (e.g. 2023: 536 buildings vs. 3,616 units) — not used here since the metric is defined as permits/buildings, not units.
